text:
alex: Starting a config-only canary now for the short-window change — adjusting routing weight and tinybatch params for traffic-sculpting. Will push to 5% of traffic for 30m.
maria: ack. which params exactly?
alex: changes: 
- route.policy: `latency_prefer` -> `cost_balanced` for tiered traffic
- batching.max_batch_size: 8 -> 6
- batching.max_wait_ms: 20 -> 15
- tenant_throttle.limit: 120/s -> 100/s for free tier
- timeout.idle_token_ms: 3000 -> 2500
(only config; no model changes)
tim: thanks — are we pinning any model versions for canary?
alex: no model pin required; this is config-only. however, we will pin routing to the canary config id so we can quickly route back to prod config if needed.
sre-oncall: please add explicit rollback guards in the playbook. suggested automatic rollback triggers: 
- error_rate_increase > 0.6% over baseline for 5m
- p95 latency increase > 30% sustained for 5m
- request queue length > 2x baseline for 5m
If any trigger fires, route 100% back to previous config and notify oncall.
anya: also add a manual pin command in the thread so we can unpin without hunting. e.g. `/config unpin route-group X`
deploy-bot: deploy initiated by alex — canary target: 5% traffic, 3 replica slices, duration: 30m. canary_id=cfg-canary-1743332100. health checks configured: 10s scrapes, 4xx/5xx rate, token-latency p95.
maria: Observability note — enable the quick eval set for chat routing (prompt-set: short-window-regression) during canary. We'll compare generation latency and token counts.
tim: Release notes snippet for the panel: "Config-only: routing policy shift for cost-balancing, reduced batch size/wait to lower tail latency; throttle lowered for free tier." Keep it short.
sre-oncall: ops checklist done? make sure CDN caches unaffected and no schema changes downstream.
alex: checklist:
- [x] infra flags applied
- [x] dashboards annotated with canary_id
- [x] alert thresholds adjusted to be conservative
- [x] release notes drafted
- [x] rollback playbook linked: https://confluence.company/ops/cfg-canary-1743332100
anya: If canary is green after 30m, plan a slow ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 60% over 3h with 30m holds. If anything odd, we abort and revert to previous config.
deploy-bot: canary progress: 1/3 slices healthy; 1 slice warming. traffic shifted 5% as requested.
maria: loading the quick eval now. I'll post a summary at the 15m mark.
sre-oncall: I'll watch SLOs and break glass if p95 > 350ms.
alex: tagging @oncall to be aware. will report back at 15m.
deploy-bot: canary heartbeat: 15m elapsed — all health checks passing. metrics snapshot: error_rate delta +0.05%, p95 latency delta +8%, token throughput -3%.
maria: quick-eval: no quality regressions on the prompt set; token usage slightly down. Looks fine so far.
tim: thumbs up. proceed with ramp plan if 30m green.
sre-oncall: still monitoring — no alerts.
alex: Great — proceeding to scheduled ramp after the 30m hold. I'll post the ramp timeline in ops calendar and update release notes with exact timing.
anya: leaving a manual unpin command here for safety: `/config rollback cfg-canary-1743332100` — can be run by eng-release leads.
maria: small suggestion for postmortem: capture the cost delta and p95 before/after for the next 24h window.
alex: will do. thanks everyone.
